passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines II
passages.text: Our knowledge of technomancy deepens. Let's improve your weaponry inside the Manaforge.

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines II
passages.text: My friend! We've secured new technology to help you bring down the Shadowguard - put it to good use!

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines III
passages.text: Our knowledge of technomancy deepens. Let's improve your weaponry inside the Manaforge.

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines III
passages.text: My friend! We've secured new technology to help you bring down the Shadowguard - put it to good use!

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines IV
passages.text: Our knowledge of technomancy deepens. Let's improve your weaponry inside the Manaforge.

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines IV
passages.text: My friend! We've secured new technology to help you bring down the Shadowguard - put it to good use!

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines V
passages.text: We've got one last upgrade to give, my friend. Come by for one last tune-up and we'll make you the strongest you've ever been!

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines V
passages.text: With this, you are as powerful as our humble band of soundrels can make you. May it serve you well against Dimensius!

passages.title: Speed Siphoner
passages.text: Great work so far! We've finished some tech that should be useful during your assault on the Manaforge.

passages.title: Speed Siphoner
passages.text: Zo'ropo brings you a new weapon. Use this to feed off of the Manaforge's arcane radiation and turn their energies against them.

passages.title: Speed Siphoner II
passages.text: We've found a way to optimize the Speed Siphoner. Come back to HQ and let me give you a boost.

passages.title: Speed Siphoner II
passages.text: Twice as fast, twice as stable. Hunt them down.

passages.title: Hacking the Mainframe
passages.text: Our saboteurs have made great progress on hacking Omega's security systems; swing by and let me tell you about what we've learned.

passages.title: Hacking the Mainframe
passages.text: There are consoles inside the Manaforge that keep the flow of energy running smoothly within the facility. We've cracked security on the first set of them, allowing you to turn the tables on enemies near Loom'ithar and Soulbinder Naazindrhi. You'll only be able to use one, but sabotaging them should allow you an edge in battle. Good luck in there.

passages.title: Hacking the Forgeweaver
passages.text: We've progressed further in our infiltration of the Manaforge's defenses. Return to HQ and I'll clear you for access.

passages.title: Hacking the Forgeweaver
passages.text: We found a weakness in Forgeweaver Araz's engineering bay that should allow you access to another console nearby. Keep up the pressure, and we'll let you know once the whole facility is ours. Happy hunting.

passages.title: Hacking the Planet
passages.text: Hero... we're in. We have full control of Manaforge Omega's security. I'll brief you on your next trip back.

passages.title: Hacking the Planet
passages.text: Manaforge Omega's security systems are under our direct control. Thanks to the damage you've done in there, we can get you access to consoles extending all the way to Salhadaar, and whatever lies beyond. We've also ensured you can use every console you come across. That's all I can do for you. Get in there and finish the fight.

passages.title: Attuned to the Aether
passages.text: Hello! I've learned valuable information about how exposure to Omega's manaflow is impacting you - let us discuss back at Shadow Point when you have a moment.

passages.title: Attuned to the Aether
passages.text: My research shows that due to the Reshii Wraps' influence on your physical form, the powerful manasurges and reactors inside Omega can be used to your benefit! While this is only a fraction of your power, it seems that arcane enhancements made to your armaments are made ever more powerful while in their vicinity. This warrants further testing...

passages.title: Order from Chaos
passages.text:
Thank you for coming to speak with me, adventurer. I know you are very busy these days.

But it is that very demand on your time that I wish to speak with you about. With all you have accomplished of late, I feel that there is bound to be some valuable data to be gleaned from your experience.

 As a <class> without equal, I would like to ask you about your deeds of late. Can you spare a moment for Moratari?

passages.title: Order from Chaos
passages.text: Once I record this data point you can return to your busy schedule.

passages.title: Order from Chaos
passages.text:
What an intriguing insight into those events.

I watched them from afar, but it is so much more fascinating to hear the version of the events as you experienced them.

Thank you for sharing that.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Loom'ithar
passages.text: Our intelligence describes a colossal beast within the Manaforge, responsible for producing the fabric that gives the Shadowguard their very form. Take it down and we'll hinder their ability to produce reinforcements. Oh, and Ba'choso says to bring some of the silk back with you - he may be able to fashion it into something useful.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Loom'ithar
passages.text: Have you procured a sample?

passages.title: Head Hunting: Loom'ithar
passages.text: Its quality is unlike anything I've ever seen! I'll get to work right away. Now, let's discuss your payment.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Forgeweaver Araz
passages.text: My friend, I hope your assault is going well. It's time for you to dispatch the Forgeweaver; using his mastery of technomancy he oversees both the Manaforge's production pipelines... as well as the ritual to return Dimensius to this plane. His workshop will be further in and heavily guarded, but cutting him down should stop their plans of resurrection for good.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Forgeweaver Araz
passages.text: Does the Forgeweaver yet live?

passages.title: Head Hunting: Forgeweaver Araz
passages.text: <name>... I should have seen that coming. His devotion to Dimensius knew no bounds, and he certainly had contingencies in place to make sure the ritual would be completed. We'll have to attack from another angle. We found some debris from his inner sanctum that made its way here - if you have the skill, we can teach you how to use it for your own ends.

passages.title: Head Hunting: The Soul Hunters
passages.text: Careful in the wastes, my friend. Scouts report that a trio of Demon Hunters are training south of the Manaforge - with one of them exhibiting power like we've never seen. You can avoid their path if you wish, but ignoring them could open you up to being flanked should they decide to engage. I recommend taking them out if you can, as well as providing us some samples of their newfound strength.

passages.title: Head Hunting: The Soul Hunters
passages.text: Soul energy like I've never seen it. While we cannot return them to the way they were, I believe you can use these runes to empower yourself even *through* death. Take them with you, and use them wisely.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Horrors of the Forge
passages.text: By now no doubt you've seen some of the Manaforge's Elite coming to Salhadaar's aid. I'm sending you a list of names now - focus on these targets, and you may uncover spoils to aid your assault.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Horrors of the Forge
passages.text: Have you eliminated your targets?

passages.title: Head Hunting: Horrors of the Forge
passages.text: Nicely done, champion. The resources they were hoarding will find a much better home with your companions.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text: The hour of Salhadaar's demise is upon us. While he may posture upon his Voidwing, he grows desperate at the feet of the All-Devouring. The army he commands is not enough for your might - strike him down.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text: Though not the end he deserved, we will celebrate his defeat nonetheless. See Zo'ropo to trade for a well-deserved reward. You have my eternal gratitude for deposing him.

passages.title: A Radiant Echo
passages.text: <Within your hand, you hold a small Azerite sphere. Its light is steady and bright, but the sound it emits is plaintive and longing. It tugs at you, ever so slightly.>

passages.title: Focusing the Energies
passages.text:
In addition to shards of nightmare, we need Blood of Sargeras to reactivate the portal to the Rift of Aln.

This rare reagent can be obtained from around the Broken Isles. Rumor has it that emissaries are in search of hardened adventurers, and may offer these in reward.

passages.title: Focusing the Energies
passages.text: Excellent, Archdruid. These will do nicely.

passages.title: Required Reagents
passages.text:
The Sentinels know of a trusted and talented enchanter who specializes in enchantments that affect demons.

She provides her services for free to the Sentinels, but she does require specific reagents to perform her enchantments.

passages.title: Required Reagents
passages.text: This should do.

passages.title: A Few Things First
passages.text:
Lately I've been working with the ore of this land, leystone it's called. I've found its qualities to hold remarkable strength and durability. We'll need a lot of it for this.

There is felslate, but that's probably too tainted for what you're looking to do with this barding.

You know, I also like to adorn my pieces with something sparkly, like a jewel. I've heard that the elves of Suramar have particularly beautiful ones. Perhaps you could acquire one for this project.

passages.title: A Few Things First
passages.text: I doubt you'll have a problem getting the leystone, but the sapphire might be a bit harder to acquire.

passages.title: A Few Things First
passages.text:
You got them! Now to upgrade your barding.

Never say a blacksmith can't improve on a leatherworker's work, I always say. I mean never. I mean... well you know what I mean.

passages.title: Blood of Sargeras
passages.text:
We will require a powerful reagent to bind the magic in our weapons and armor. A rare material that will do just the trick is Blood of Sargeras.

We will need a plentiful quantity. Bring me whatever you can muster.

passages.title: Blood of Sargeras
passages.text: Yes, this is just what we need to complete our preparations. These must have been difficult to come by. Thank you, Highlord.

passages.title: Noggenfogger's Reasonable Request
passages.text:
Oh, the gall of that little green twerp! Marin Noggenfogger is blackmailing us. He says that if we do not meet his "very reasonable requisition request", he is going to close off access to the crucible.

Marin's asking for a hefty amount of Aethril. He said something about you recently holding a blade to his throat and that he's simply returning the favor.

Of course, if you would rather, I can eliminate him.

passages.title: Noggenfogger's Reasonable Request
passages.text:
No hard feelings, right? Business is business, baby, and business is good. I saw an opportunity and I took it, just like you.

To show my continued allegiance with your little organization, and as a gesture of goodwill, here's a little sample of the product. It's magic. Bottoms up!

passages.title: Saltheril's Haven
passages.text:
<name>, I presume? Very good. Your reputation precedes you.

Lord Saltheril sends his most sincere greetings, along with a cordial invitation to join him at his estate south of Silvermoon.

A portion of the grounds have been carved out as a decadent haven for those seeking refined company and pleasant conversation. He believes you would bring a... unique perspective.

<He looks you over with a hint of polite disdain.>

Receiving an invitation is a rare honor. His lordship hopes you will accept.

passages.title: Saltheril's Haven
passages.text:
Ah, <name>. Welcome to my Haven--a sanctuary from the world's turmoil since the days of Anasterian.

Some presume this to be merely a frivolous party, but on these beautiful gilded grounds, decisions have been made over wine that have shaped the fates of entire generations.

passages.title: Honored Guests
passages.text:
I am pleased you could join us. Today marks the start of a very special occasion.

The sin'dorei are no strangers to the war table, but its aristocracy prefers to play more coy. In wartime, the crown sends representatives to curry favor with the nobles. If they are pleased, they might lend gold to the war effort.

It is very much like courting a lover, with all the jealous games you might imagine.

So let us play the game, shall we? Deliver these invitations while we finish preparations here.

passages.title: Honored Guests
passages.text: Your presence is already turning heads. This will be quite the spectacle.

passages.title: Honored Guests
passages.text:
Ah, so the rumors are true about your efficiency.

Excellent. Now we can begin the game.

passages.title: High Esteem
passages.text:
Invitations to my Haven are highly exclusive, especially at a time like this. Extending an offer, even a temporary one, is a great honor.

My favor carries quite a bit of weight amongst the aristocracy. If I invite an ally of one of our representatives, it suggests I think highly of them--and if I think highly of them, so too will our noble guests.

But is it not terribly fun if I let you choose an invitation instead?

Go peruse any enticements they may offer, then make your selection.

passages.title: High Esteem
passages.text: Pick any invitation you desire.

passages.title: High Esteem
passages.text: I will have my valet send for them at once.

passages.title: Embrace Your Own Legend
passages.text:
I will keep a close eye on your progress and watch your exploits with that artifact unfold with great interest.

Once you have embraced the power of your own legend, I would like to hear your perspective on how important the artifact you wield has been on your journey.

passages.title: Embrace Your Own Legend
passages.text: We are on a journey of learning and discovery. Let us walk it together.

passages.title: Embrace Your Own Legend
passages.text:
You have grown stronger, but your artifact is stronger yet.

It would appear that my hypothesis holds true--artifacts appear to be the key to protecting Azeroth.

passages.title: The Vanishing of Iridikron
passages.text:
As you traveled through Zaralek caverns, Chronormu and I confronted Iridikron and the Infinite Dragonflight.

While we defeated the Infinite Dragonflight's champion, Chrono-Lord Deios, I fear Iridikron escaped.

Allow me to show you what happened, for it gives us a clue of what must be done next.

passages.title: The Vanishing of Iridikron
passages.text:
What Iridikron plans to do with that artifact is beyond my vision.

We must focus on Vyrakk and Vyranoth for now.

passages.title: The Subtle Game
passages.text:
Appearances are everything. If the court sees that I favor a certain group, they will follow suit.

Take these tokens of my favor and hand them out to our honored guests as you see fit. I suspect they may invite you to partake in their plans and share in the profits, if you choose to align yourself with their cause.

passages.title: The Subtle Game
passages.text: Do endeavor not to keep our guests waiting in suspense.

passages.title: The Subtle Game
passages.text:
Splendid.

I dearly hope you find some time to enjoy yourself while court is in season. While I do appreciate the sullen, results-driven sort, you could stand to smile.

passages.title: Tracking Down Incarnates
passages.text:
We must turn our attention to Fyrakk and Vyranoth with Iridikron seemingly vanished from our sight.

Merithra and the Green Dragonflight have been pursuing him and have a lead. 

They've received the aid of Shandris Feathermoon in this task.

She awaits you within Valdrakken. Shandris will need your help with what is to come.

passages.title: Tracking Down Incarnates
passages.text:
Ah, <name>. I was about to send a messenger to find you.

I suppose this is Nozdormu's doing. The Bronze Dragonflight do tend to be proactive.

Let's get started.

passages.title: Surpass Your Own Legend
passages.text:
While artifacts are key, we must not dismiss the power of the individuals who wield them.

Continue in your fight against the Legion. Grow strong, stronger than you ever thought possible.

Then we will compare the might of your legend against that of the artifact.

passages.title: Surpass Your Own Legend
passages.text:
The person wielding an artifact is of some importance. But how much? Which legend is the greater?

Let us find out together.

passages.title: Surpass Your Own Legend
passages.text: I admit. I am pleasantly surprised to be proven wrong. Your power has grown and I cannot say with certainty which is the greater. You, or the weapon you wield.

passages.title: Shape a New Legend
passages.text:
It is clear now that the person is at least as important as the artifact they wield.

Perhaps it is the quality of mortality that diminishes the importance of the individual through the lens of history. While an artifact is eternal, the people wielding them are fleeting.

But no flame that burns brightly burns forever.

I want you to burn as brightly as you can. Empower your artifact and carve a new legend into the world for all to see.

passages.title: Shape a New Legend
passages.text: An artifact cannot empower itself. Its power grows only when its wielder performs great deeds with it.

passages.title: Shape a New Legend
passages.text:
Humbling.

It is the very nature of finite existence that is the answer.

Mortality is the flame that shines brightest because it is free to choose a single moment of glory, rather than be burdened by the weight of eternity.

Choose your moment well, <name>, and nothing, not even time, will be able to stop you.

passages.title: Unstoppable Force
passages.text:
This statue seems out of place here. Nothing else like it. But this is where Anduin Lothar fell against Orgrim Doomhammer at the Battle of Blackrock Mountain.

Many fought on this field. Many didn't make it. Lothar... 

Let me tell ye what happened all those years ago.

passages.title: Unstoppable Force
passages.text: It was such a dark day, <name>. Painful to remember.

passages.title: Unstoppable Force
passages.text:
It's a tragic story, but maybe something better can be made o' it with those fragments of Turalyon's shield.

Perhaps it can be restored--along with our friend.

passages.title: Suramar Liberated
passages.text:
You have come a long way, adventurer. I never seem to tire of following your exploits. Even from afar, as a silent observer, I find myself absolutely invested in what you will do next.

I do have one question though.

passages.title: Suramar Liberated
passages.text:
Very intriguing.

I will, of course, record that as a data point.

Knowing how you decide on a course of action will inform further hypothesis.

passages.title: Armies Gathered
passages.text:
The stakes have never been higher than now, adventurer.

I would very much like to know what you are thinking right now.

passages.title: Armies Gathered
passages.text:
Fresh insights are invaluable in our efforts here, <name>.

Thank you for sharing yours.

passages.title: Azeroth Saved
passages.text:
adventurer.

You have done it! Sargeras is gone and Azeroth is saved.

I can only imagine what must be going through your mind at this moment.

Let us remedy that.

Allow me to record your thoughts and your words. Not as written by a historian who you never met, but by a friend who wished nothing more than to listen.

passages.title: Azeroth Saved
passages.text: Too many histories are written about the WHAT, the WHY, the HOW, and the WHEN. Other than names, however, we so rarely get to truly know the WHO.

passages.title: Until Our Next Hello
passages.text:
Well, the moment is fast approaching now.

<Moratari subtly nods in the direction of the raging temporal storm overhead.>

You would think after so many goodbyes I would be better at this, but alas, I simply prefer hello over goodbye. I know a lot of people around here are going to miss you too.

You should go say goodbye to them while there is still time.

passages.title: Until Our Next Hello
passages.text:
There. That was not so bad after all.

This is not goodbye. It is just a pause until our next hello.

I look forward to it, <name>.

passages.title: Sweating Mana
passages.text: Default Description

passages.title: Ethereal Delves
passages.text:
There's even more tae do in delves, <name>! 

Meet me in Dornogal. There's loads to discuss!

passages.title: Ethereal Delves
passages.text: Good tae see ye! We've got plenty tae discuss.

passages.title: Disrupt the Call
passages.text:
We do not know where they intend to strike, but we do know they aim to summon more to their cause.

Destroy the Twilight's Blade before they complete their rituals. We must not let a single champion of the void remain to inspire the new recruits.

passages.title: Disrupt the Call
passages.text: There is much to do. Do not dawdle.

passages.title: Disrupt the Call
passages.text: These champions of the Twilight's Blade are just as foolhardy as the other members of the cult. We will cut them all down, in time.

passages.title: Guardians Must Go
Bring Back De Bones
passages.text:
Big thanks for breakin' us free. Some were not so lucky.

Bring dey bones back to de Chief, he will know what to do.

passages.title: De Vile Diminished
passages.text:
These vile orbs are harvestin' de souls of our people and sendin' dark energy to de Knife Priestess. She's gettin' mighty powerful.

Destroy de orbs so her ritual of death is ruined. With de gift of Shadra, ya will not fail.

passages.title: De Vile Diminished
passages.text: Did ya find all de orbs?

passages.title: De Vile Diminished
passages.text:
Do ya sense it? De death energy dat was oozin' about de place feels thin.

It will take but a breath to end dis ritual for good.

passages.title: One Will Not Rise
passages.text:
Now's our best shot! We end de sacrifices here! Stoppin' de dark energy has weakened her hold.

Then, you can be de one to bring back her head.

Uh, and <name>--no tellin' de chief about me callin' him Big VunVun. He'll be turnin' me into a frog if he hears dat again.

passages.title: One Will Not Rise
passages.text: I am pleased you're takin' my words so literally.

passages.title: One Will Not Rise
passages.text:
Ah! My day's gettin' better already! De Witherbark are grateful, <name>.

Dak'zor didn't say... nevermind. I don't wanna know.

passages.title: Disarm the Dark Horde
passages.text:
The Dark Horde have no love fer their equipment. Look at their weapons! Cracked, rusted, blunt, and bent. Ach!

The only way they function is by making more shoddy tools to constantly replace the ones they've broken.

If ye see any of their weapon racks, destroy 'em. Let's see how well they fight without their rusty blades.

A bare-fisted orc is nothing to sneeze at, but it'll further delay any daft plans they've got.

passages.title: Disarm the Dark Horde
passages.text:
Did ye destroy their weapons racks?

Aye, that'll do. We've bought everyone nearby a few months of peace while they resupply.

passages.title: Recap: The Harbinger
passages.text: To understand the story of The War Within, one must first begin with the mysterious entity known as the Harbinger, and how the heroes of Azeroth uncovered the truth...

passages.title: Recap: The Harbinger
passages.text: Xal'atath was a mysterious foe with ties to the Void. Her presence portended dire things for Azeroth...

passages.title: Recap: The Harbinger
passages.text: Alleria uncovered the mystery of the Harbinger, revealing Xal'atath. However, it would not be long before the Harbinger made her move.

passages.title: Deepening Shadows
passages.text:
Champion, I could use your assistance. The natives here in Silvermoon are proving to be less hospitable than we had hoped. 

In their defense, their city is facing down a darkness unlike anything Azeroth has ever faced, so tensions are high.

Can you use your unique perspective and help de-escalate some of the hot spots that are emerging around Silvermoon?

passages.title: Deepening Shadows
passages.text: Tensions are high.

passages.title: Deepening Shadows
passages.text:
Well done. That Voidstorm is evoking fear and terror in everyone who sees it, myself included. 

But I chose this life of standing up to evil and spitting in its face. Sadly not everyone had the luxury of that being a choice.

passages.title: Recap: Fractured Visions
passages.text: All across Azeroth, many were having visions of a Radiant Song. Efforts to understand what seemed to be a warning centered on the heroes in Dalaran.

passages.title: Recap: Fractured Visions
passages.text: The island of Khaz Algar figured into Xal'atath's plans, and it was up to the champions of Azeroth to thwart them.

passages.title: Catch Up: Khaz Algar
Catch Up: The Ringing Deeps
Catch Up: Hallowfall
Recap: Shadowy Pursuits
passages.text: King Anduin Wrynn, Alleria, and the champions travel deeper into Azeroth, arriving at a place known as Hallowfall. It quickly becomes apparent that this place has also been touched by the machinations of Xal'atath.

passages.title: Recap: Shadowy Pursuits
passages.text: With a few select allies, Anduin, Alleria, and the champions escaped Xal'atath's clutches, but this would not be the last encounter with her...

passages.title: Catch Up: A Light in the Dark
Recap: The Dark Heart
passages.text: The champions and Alleria were invited to Undermine by Gazlowe as the peoples of Khaz Algar and beyond began to unite against Xal'atath and her Dark Heart.

passages.title: Recap: The Dark Heart
passages.text: Dimensius was defeated and Azeroth was saved from his threat, yet there was a cost.

passages.title: Recap: The Dark Heart
passages.text: This is the conclusion of The War Within, but it is not the last time we'll see Xal'atath or the Dark Heart...

passages.title: Drain You
passages.text:
Do you... see...? They follow... They plead... for help...

<The voidwalker strains and shudders as it tries to communicate.>

Too weak... too starving...

<It feebly hands you a shard of dark matter.>

This... will feed me... then together... we find the missing elves...

passages.title: Drain You
passages.text:
I am better now... stable, but a fatigue still clings to me.

If we're to find your scouts, I will need your help.

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text:
My Shadowtrade Mercenaries will fight for Stormarion Cores, no questions asked, but they do get hungry also!

Food is quite scarce here, so we need supplies!

Take a mercenary out with you and find some food for them to eat. I'll make it worth your while!

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: Is that mercenary well fed?

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: When it comes to mercenaries, nothing keeps them loyal like a full stomach... and gold.

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text:
My Shadowtrade Mercenaries will fight for Stormarion Cores, no questions asked, but they do get hungry also!

Food is quite scarce here, so we need supplies!

Take a mercenary out with you and find some food for them to eat. I'll make it worth your while!

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: Is that mercenary well fed?

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: When it comes to mercenaries, nothing keeps them loyal like a full stomach... and gold.

passages.title: Just Between Us
passages.text:
The artifact we snatched from the timeline earlier was replaced with a simulacrum so none would notice the true artifact's absence.

Such a wealth of infinite energy should not be abandoned so readily. You should seek it out and reclaim it.

Once you have recovered the simulacrum you can scrap it for an embarassing sum of bronze and infinite power.

passages.title: Just Between Us
passages.text:
Success!

It's almost a shame to destroy such a beautiful replica.

But you have the real thing, so I say scrap it and rejoice at the bounty of beautiful bronze!

passages.title: Welcome Home
passages.text:
What a mess! Perhaps the previous owners left in a hurry. Best tidy up!

The items removed will be sent to the house chest. They can always be placed down again, if cobwebs are your thing.

passages.title: Time to Decorate
passages.text:
Now that we've got this place tidied up, let's decorate!

The community has chipped in with donations to make sure you have plenty of options to work with.

Let's have a look!

passages.title: Hitting the Hammer
passages.text:
The Twilight Hammer is dirtying up the ruins of Zeb'tala. Clean up the area and bring back some of their personal tokens. One never knows what curiosities may appeal to those vying for relevancy.

Those mindless cultists may stomp around and act tough, but you will make quick work of them.

passages.title: Hitting the Hammer
passages.text: Have you found anything useful?

passages.title: Hitting the Hammer
passages.text:
You have successfully blunted those Twilight tools. Whether or not we will have any takers for this odd assortment of tokens is yet to be determined.

There is, however, no accounting for taste.

passages.title: Hold the Watch
passages.text:
There is still a lot of friction on the border with Zul'Aman, but we must hold the watch on all fronts.

Check in with Bloodguard Nelric at the Thalassian Pass. It is rumored to be one of the most uneventful posts. I am certain he would appreciate a reprieve, if only for a few moments.

Stay alert, adventurer!

passages.title: Hold the Watch
passages.text:
An uneventful watch is more rewarding than an empty conversation.

The Blood Knights appreciate your service.

passages.title: Naga Blades
passages.text:
It seems the locals currently find great appeal in naga blades--the brinier the better. On our southwestern shore, you will find the Daggerspine naga.

They have these grungy, barnacle-encrusted scimitars that would perfectly fit the bill.

Go grab a few of those. They could have value in some of our upcoming discussions.

passages.title: Naga Blades
passages.text: Were you able to procure some blades?

passages.title: Naga Blades
passages.text:
Excellent work! These will do nicely.

Between us, my personal preference leans toward the colorful seashells. Maybe that is because my sword is more than an adornment.

passages.title: Sunfire to the Blade
passages.text:
I guess there is one benefit to being part of the courtly intrigue: one does hear things. We have this concoction of sunfire infused with the holy energy of the Blood Knights, courtesy of the court alchemists.

Take this down to the Sanctum of the Moon and test it on the Twilight intruders. I look forward to hearing the results in detail.

passages.title: Sunfire to the Blade
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Sunfire to the Blade
passages.text: Anar'anel belore! You love to hear it. This news is sure to warm a few hearts for our cause.

passages.title: That's Our Wood
passages.text:
It seems the lure of the lightwood continues to be a problem.

We may as well take advantage of the trolls' hard work! Collect what they have harvested. We can make use of it.

What we do not use for weapons, we can hand over to the carvers. The nobles will clamor over lightwood decor.

passages.title: That's Our Wood
passages.text: Did you gather the lightwood?

passages.title: That's Our Wood
passages.text:
Your task is done. These will prove useful.

Do not let on that the Blood Knights got first pick.

passages.title: Lightbloom Dimmed
passages.text:
All of this small talk makes my ears twitch. I would be so much more useful doing field work. For now, you get to do the fun part.

The creatures within the Lightbloom are getting a bit dense. I need you to get out there and lower the volume.

I am sure you'll run into many options while you are out there. Take a whack at a few for me.

passages.title: Lightbloom Dimmed
passages.text:
You have performed well. Silvermoon appreciates your service.

I would have happily swapped places with you, but we all have our assignments.

passages.title: Less Lawless
passages.text:
The Tideborne are always running just over the legal line. They are an annoyance at best, but will push boundaries when given too much rope.

The ones in Sunsail Anchorage made the mistake of ripping off some nobles not too long ago. Maybe go smack them around a bit--remind them to respect their betters.

passages.title: Less Lawless
passages.text: Have you taught the Tideborne a lesson?

passages.title: Less Lawless
passages.text:
Ah, that must have been such fun! My bar may be lower today, after the engrossing discourse on the harvesting cycle of the basic peacebloom.

Apologies. Know your service is appreciated.

passages.title: Taxing the Tideborne
passages.text:
Have you ever noticed, that sometimes there is benefit in letting someone think they are getting away with something? The Tideborne will continue to smuggle in plain sight, feeling clever at the taxes they're avoiding paying to Silvermoon.

This does add up, though, over time. When you have a moment, please head down to the harbor and relieve them of some of their back taxes.

passages.title: Taxing the Tideborne
passages.text: Is it still stealing when stolen from thieves?

passages.title: Taxing the Tideborne
passages.text:
One must appreciate the special jingle of a heavy sack of purloined coins.

Excellent work, my friend.

passages.title: Chop It Down
passages.text:
We received word there's a creature from Lightbloom Ath'Ran making trouble on the western coast. It has caused a bit of drama.

Head over and resolve the issue.

passages.title: Chop It Down
passages.text: Is the issue resolved?

passages.title: Chop It Down
passages.text: Good work. I'm sure that will make for some excellent kindling.

passages.title: Lovely Plumage
passages.text:
The beautiful members of the Silvermoon Court do so love their colorful embellishments.

For this, we can stock up while doing a good deed! Head over to Thuron's Livery and pick up some of the brightly colored feathers shed from the hawkstriders in training.

Vaelith gets clean up service and we get the lovely plumage.

passages.title: Lovely Plumage
passages.text: Did you find loads of feathers?

passages.title: Lovely Plumage
passages.text:
You are so good at this!

One of these days, we should pile these feathers up and let everyone jump in them. I think you would be surprised how many proper lords and ladies would gleefully participate.

For now, we will explore feathery accents.

passages.title: Sungrub Silk
passages.text:
Oh, adventurer, have you ever visited the Solaarian Sunbath? If not, it's highly recommended.

The sungrubs that wander nearby have a precious silk from which amazing fabric can be made. Solwin Brightstitch is reputed to be masterful in this, with his sartorial magic.

The raw materials are often sought out to have him create unique and personalized goods from scratch. Bring us some of that lovely silk. It will provide a soft cushion when faced with harder discussions.

passages.title: Sungrub Silk
passages.text: Oh, did you get all of the silk?

passages.title: Sungrub Silk
passages.text:
Perfect! I have to confess, it will be hard to give some of this up.

I must remember, I have a job to do here. It can't all be fun and games.

Your work is appreciated.

passages.title: Windrunner Memorabilia
passages.text:
The nobles do so love the unusual. Take a look around Windrunner Village. There are sure to be some interesting mementos still tucked away there.

I will find an advantageous home for the pieces you bring back.

passages.title: Windrunner Memorabilia
passages.text: Did you find anything interesting?

passages.title: Windrunner Memorabilia
passages.text:
I asked for unusual and you delivered! A couple of these seem a bit... suspect.

I'm sure it will be fine. What could go wrong with items of mysterious origin?

passages.title: Put a Little Snap in Their Step
passages.text:
Those naga are, as ever, being a beachfront nuisance. Do they not understand that is a prime location?

We may not be able to reliably drive them off, but a little mischief would not be untoward.

I found this tune that drives the snapdragons mad. They will just attack whoever is nearby. Take this and give it a shot!

passages.title: Put a Little Snap in Their Step
passages.text: Are the naga adequately harassed?

passages.title: Put a Little Snap in Their Step
passages.text:
I feel bad for the snapdragons, but I can't help but laugh at the look of surprise on their face when their little buddies pounce on them.

Thank you for making the day a little more entertaining.

passages.title: Potted Lashers
passages.text:
It seems some of the nobles are botany-curious where the Lightbloom is concerned. They seek the exotic to adorn their windowsills and lurk in the dangerous section of their greenhouses.

That's where you come in, adventurer!

Go harvest those small and pernicious plants. Their bulbs will be the best for planting.

passages.title: Potted Lashers
passages.text: Any problems with the harvest?

passages.title: Potted Lashers
passages.text:
The results of sharing these with the Silvermoon elite could range from passably amusing to disastrous.

Either way, I look forward to seeing the results of their gardening efforts.

passages.title: Brightwing Conservation
passages.text:
The conservators at Brightwing Estate have a mischievous young dragonhawk named Cerul that likes to run away whenever their backs are turned. He doesn't go far, but it has become a game for him to get them to chase him.

Take this delicious treat with you and use it to lure him back home.

passages.title: Brightwing Conservation
passages.text:
It makes everyone happy to have all the creatures home at Brightwing. Having a peaceful place to enjoy the coast is a benefit to all.

Thank you for letting Cerul enjoy a little play time!

passages.title: Ghostland Peppers
passages.text:
The delicate blue ghostland peppers may not look like much, but they have a mean burn. Many nobles won't admit it, but they are quite popular in the noble games of "Truth or Challenge."

Please procure a few for me. I like to watch them sweat.

passages.title: Ghostland Peppers
passages.text: How goes the harvest?

passages.title: Ghostland Peppers
passages.text:
Joy! These will bring much excitement, and some chagrin, to the court.

Many thanks! Oh, and <name>... be sure to cleanse your hands before you rub your eyes--or worse. I learned that the hard way.

passages.title: Sunset to Sea
passages.text:
Naga have set up camp on the Sunset Strand. The sunset slugs that called it home are distraught and seem unsure what to do. This little tune will remind them of their home.

Go inspire them to seek the freedom of the open sea.

passages.title: Sunset to Sea
passages.text:
Best of luck to our little nudibranchian friends! Yes, I made that word up, but is it not accurate?

Thank you for helping them seek out more pleasant waters.

passages.title: A Little Errand
passages.text:
When conversations get tense, it can be challenging to keep words flowing in a productive way. At times like these, I find a little social lubrication is in order.

Swing over to Goldenmist Village and pick up a cask of Vintner's Golden. It's proven to have a euphoric side effect that can be quite helpful.

passages.title: A Little Errand
passages.text: Did you find the cask?

passages.title: A Little Errand
passages.text: Perfect! This is just what the court ordered.

passages.title: Where Has the Wine Gone?
passages.text:
I entrusted one of my apprentices with the delivery of several cases of particularly expensive wine. He was to bring them here from my private storage, but he has not yet arrived.

I should hate to ask you to retrieve him, but I cannot stress enough how expensive those bottles are.

Please see if you can locate him and my delivery. He should have been traveling from the north to arrive here.

passages.title: Where Has the Wine Gone?
passages.text: I dearly hope my apprentice has a colorful excuse for his tardiness.

passages.title: Where Has the Wine Gone?
passages.text:
The wine attacked you both, you say? Ah yes, I suppose the mana in that particular vintage is prone to sedimentation.

I am pleased most of it was recoverable.

passages.title: Diminutive Demand
passages.text:
Keeping preciously small animals as pets is a popular pastime among the nobility. The more unconventional the animal, often obtained through magic, the more of a conversation piece it is.

I have enchanted this wand with the appropriate shrinking spell. Use it on some of the colorful toads out near the ponds and bring them back here. The nobles will find them delightful.

Naturally, the toads may not take kindly to the enchantment. But I trust you can handle that, should it occur.

passages.title: Diminutive Demand
passages.text: Fear not. The enchantment is quite permanent.

passages.title: Diminutive Demand
passages.text:
Oh, they are positively precious, are they not?

I imagine we will see quite a few miniscule toads in handbags this coming season.

passages.title: Pyrepetal Purposes
passages.text:
Lord Saltheril, that old lynx, has put me in a bit of a bind.

He has requested a grand fireworks display to accompany tonight's dinner service, but we are dreadfully low on pyrepetal dust. It is an herb native to Eversong, highly flammable and quite dazzling when set aflame by pyromancy.

Could you help us replenish our stores? We mostly harvest it from the woods near Scintilas Falls.

passages.title: Pyrepetal Purposes
passages.text: Do be careful to keep the pyrepetals away from open flame.

passages.title: Pyrepetal Purposes
passages.text: Wonderful. This quantity should be sufficient for a lovely round of fireworks.

passages.title: What Horrible Magic
passages.text:
Have you seen the encampments the naga have been constructing along our coast? Dreadful business.

Not only do they menace our ships and disrupt our trade routes, but they might pose a real threat to Eversong's inland settlements if allowed to continue operations unchecked.

Their arcanists are particularly dangerous. Dispose of them and our guests will be in your debt.

passages.title: What Horrible Magic
passages.text: I trust this task is within your skill set.

passages.title: What Horrible Magic
passages.text: Marvelous. I am certain our guests would have preferred to see the battle themselves, but tales of your heroism will do nicely.

passages.title: Fit for a Magister
passages.text:
Battle prowess and magical skill are important, of course, but one cannot deny the power of appearances. A well-dressed army instills far more faith than one bedecked in rags.

Fortunately, a fine set of robes can be both flattering and functional. The mana silk produced at the North Sanctum can be woven into robes that deepen and intensify our magical reserves.

Be a dear and gather some for us, would you? My wardrobe could use a seasonal refreshment.

passages.title: Fit for a Magister
passages.text: Do be careful around the mana wyrms. I understand they can be aggressive after harvesting.

passages.title: Fit for a Magister
passages.text:
Mana silk has a beautiful sheen, does it not?

The Magisters will be looking spectacular throughout the soiree.

passages.title: Power Clean
passages.text:
The festivities have been wonderfully entertaining, which means the nobles have been leaving a bit of a mess around the estate. Lord Saltheril's servants have been keeping up with the cleaning, but the Magisters could lend a hand.

Enchanting a few brooms to sweep the pavilion should be an easy but impressive feat.

I was informed that an arcanist was employing the same tactic over at Farstrider Hold. Go retrieve some of his brooms and I will have them re-enchanted here.

passages.title: Power Clean
passages.text: Technically any broom would do, but the magic is easier to weave if the object has already been primed to receive the enchantment.

passages.title: Power Clean
passages.text: We will have the estate shining in no time.

passages.title: A Bit of Bloodthistle
passages.text:
You know, I bring Saltheril a lot of "imported" wine, but one of the first things I started supplying him with was bloodthistle. It's an herb that only grows around Eversong. It's got a smooth bite to it, sort of like mana. Nice and classy. His parties really go through the stuff.

I took a look and I don't think he has enough to last this whole thing. We should get some more.

The best stuff grows over by the West Sanctum. Grab as much as you can carry. Trust me--it'll go fast.

passages.title: A Bit of Bloodthistle
passages.text: Trust me. I know how to keep nobles happy.

passages.title: A Bit of Bloodthistle
passages.text:
Nice haul. You've got a good eye for this stuff.

If you're ever looking for work after this thing's over, let me know.

passages.title: Still Behind Enemy Portals
passages.text:
In our reminiscing of past events, we were reminded of an artifact that we did not recover during our war with the Burning Legion.

This item is a vessel of great evil, and should not stay in the clutches of the remaining demonic forces.

To reach this item, we must journey to the Broken Shore where Tehd has a portal he has repurposed for our use. Will you join us on this hunt?

passages.title: Still Behind Enemy Portals
passages.text: We should have recovered this the first time.

passages.title: Still Behind Enemy Portals
passages.text: You found the vessel, I see. Good. We will take it and make sure it gets into the right hands.

passages.title: A Frostbitten Tally
passages.text:
Tarenar and I heard stories about the invasion of Icecrown Citadel from all the way out in the Plaguelands.

But he's got it all wrong!

The elf thinks there were more Ebon Blade commanders than Argent Crusade in the Ashen Verdict. He's completely daft. Obviously there were more paladins!

Would you go poke around Icecrown Citadel and find me some proof? I'm sick of arguing with him!

passages.title: A Frostbitten Tally
passages.text: You find anything yet? Just need something to prove to Tarenar that I'm right.

passages.title: A Frostbitten Tally
passages.text:
Och, these tabards are looking worse for wear. I guess it's hard to say who showed up in greater force from some old relics.

Anyway, we're on to arguing which of us slept the least while on the Broken Shore.

Looks like you managed to snag an Ebon Blade banner and are still alive to tell the tale. There is a spot nearby to hang that up in the Arcantina.

passages.title: Timear Foresees a Proof of Demise!
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. Do you have a moment?

There's something important I lost during the assault on the Isle of Thunder: a pocket watch gifted to me by my old friend, Archmage Timear. Yes, that Timear... the one that can foresee the future. He told me this day would come and that you would assist me.

The watch was taken by the Council of Elders, specifically by High Priestess Mar'li. If you would go to the island and retrieve it from the Throne of Thunder, and we both know you will, I can get you there.

passages.title: Timear Foresees a Proof of Demise!
passages.text:
Was Timear's prognostication correct? Have you retrieved my pocket watch?

Or have you simply returned to enjoy my scintillating company?

passages.title: Timear Foresees a Proof of Demise!
passages.text:
Of course you were successful. Timear's insufferably always correct about these things. And, he has returned to rub my nose in it.

You have my gratitude.

It appears you've also found an Ancient Zandalari Scroll. Timear has already foresaw it being displayed in the Arcantina. Take a look around for where to put it.

passages.title: Where the Fire Once Burned
passages.text:
Hard to believe, isn't it? Horde and Alliance, same room, no stabbing.

I was reminiscing about my days in the Firelands, gathering luciferns. They had such a distinctive smell... somewhere between smoke and something long dead. It's been a while, and I almost miss it.

Grab a few for Zen'tabra and me, will you? She deserves the full experience.

passages.title: Where the Fire Once Burned
passages.text: I hope you found those luciferns--because if not, I get stabby. Very stabby.

passages.title: Where the Fire Once Burned
passages.text:
It's strange how a single scent can bring back so many memories. Thank you for letting me share this.

And... apologies to everyone else. Some memories are meant to linger.

You found an evergreen vine in the Firelands? If that isn't a sign of hope, I don't know what is.

Stick it in the Arcantina--it might be the first plant in here that doesn't immediately give up.

passages.title: Uncrowned's Cold Case
passages.text:
We are lucky the Uncrowned survived, and its archives, thanks to Taoshi. We've been reading them...

Have you heard of the great highborne city Dire Maul? The Uncrowned kept tabs on the dangerous prince, Tortheldrin, but since he died, the case was shelved.

These notes say there might be objects of interest in the city ruins, with a notable mention of Nostro's Compendium of Dragon Slaying. That book was retrieved some time ago, but few know that several chapters were missing.

Let's reopen the case.

passages.title: Uncrowned's Cold Case
passages.text:
Surrounded by hearth and friends, it's hard to believe Dalaran is truly gone... 

<Kelsey looks at Taoshi with deep sincerity.>

The Uncrowned wastes no time picking up its affairs. Have you found anything of interest?

passages.title: Uncrowned's Cold Case
passages.text:
What a surprise! I thought anything like this would have been thoroughly scavenged and carried far, far away by now.

I'll find someone to work on those pages. Many scribes would be delighted to have the opportunity to translate ancient magic.

And you came back with the Pylon Fragment too? So you went into Dire Maul. What a fine memento for future visitors to inquire about. 

Consider putting it somewhere in the Arcantina.

passages.title: Hellscream's Heritage
passages.text:
My sister Krenna was once a Conqueror in the Horde's armies. Ruthless. Brutal. Some said a tyrant. But she was different when we were young. Scared, but always kind to me. Warm to those she would let in. Did power change her? 

And if it changed her into a tyrant, did it change Garrosh Hellscream as well? I know who Krenna was. I do not know who Garrosh was. 

Travel to Nagrand and find out.

passages.title: Hellscream's Heritage
passages.text: I would know who the previous leader of the Warsong really was.

passages.title: Hellscream's Heritage
passages.text:
Hellscream had no strength, so he built it. He had no pride, until it was given to him. Yet... he was this way, strong-willed and resilient, all along.

Then perhaps power does not change a person--it simply reveals who they really are, deep within. 

This Greatmother Geyah is wise. I should visit her someday.

You also brought back a tome that looks like it has seen better days. I can imagine the vast knowledge within it. 

Its rightful place is here in the Arcantina. Please find a safe location for it.

passages.title: The Fragrance of the Dunes
passages.text:
I miss the smell of the desert. It is the fragrance of freedom in a wild land. I would love to refresh that scent memory.

While you're there, grab something from the caravans. This place could use some nomad personality.

Maybe hop over to Shatterstone Harbor and get something for the big guy. Maybe an anchor? That would be perfect! Imagine watching him lug that around.

passages.title: The Fragrance of the Dunes
passages.text: Did you fill the pouch?

passages.title: The Fragrance of the Dunes
passages.text:
Ah! Just breathe that in, <name>. 

Thank you for taking me back to another time... and home.

Hang up that tapestry, would you? I would like to introduce my friends in the Arcantina to the finest of vulpera weaving.

passages.title: A Generational Moment
passages.text:
It's always good to see someone with your history continue to speak to us old dogs, adventurer.

Eitrigg and I have been talking about legacy recently. Did you know we both fought with the Valarjar against the Legion? Interesting how long histories can intertwine.

But our real legacy is our children. I wonder if you would have time to check in with them both. While you're there, make sure they're keeping their skills sharp.

passages.title: A Generational Moment
passages.text: Were you able to find Lorna? What of Eitrigg's son Ariok?

passages.title: A Generational Moment
passages.text:
I can tell by the look on your face that our children gave a proper account for themselves.

It's good to know that, should they face further danger, their skills are still sharp.

Looks like you found a clefthoof hide while you were in the Blasted Lands. 

Eitrigg would know better than I, but that must have came through the Dark Portal from Draenor.

That's something to display, and I can't think of a better place than right here in the Arcantina.

passages.title: Turbo-Boost: Trade Must Flow
passages.text:
<The Trust is under pressure from the cartels to keep markets open. We seek associates capable of removing certain... obstacles. Cartel So has been authorized to distribute substantial riches if you are successful.

Complete the task, and collect a special reward from Fixer So'kir outside of the Dornogal Treasury. Parties shall remain unbound by any implied oaths arising in the course of trade. Uniform Broker Code standard terms apply.>

passages.title: Turbo-Boost: Trade Must Flow
passages.text:
The Trust thanks you for your assistance, <name>. 

As promised, here is your reward. 

To celebrate the success of our new partnership, we are including a small performance bonus. Please return later for more work!

passages.title: Dawnstar Defense
passages.text:
The nearby runestone has gone dark, and the Lightbloom is on its way. I can't hold this ground alone. Help me set the weapons, line up the potions, and get our supplies in order.

We'll meet that growth with discipline and precision and send it back in pieces.

passages.title: Dawnstar Defense
passages.text: Have you finished setting up?

passages.title: Dawnstar Defense
passages.text: Good work. Now for the hard part.

passages.title: And Then They Came
passages.text:
Brace yourself--the time is upon us!

Hold the line and keep them from reaching the runestone at all costs. I'll focus on restoring its power, but I need you to protect me and everyone here.

Are you ready?

passages.title: And Then They Came
passages.text: The runestone hums with power again thanks to you. You have my appreciation.

passages.title: Hidey-Hole
passages.text:
When Xal'atath departed she left behind a large number of anomalies, small pocket dimensions where enemies can hide. As Romuul calls them, "Hidey-Holes".

The Artificer has rigged up a device that should do the job.

We need to close these Hidey-Holes and flush out any enemies lurking inside.

passages.title: Hidey-Hole
passages.text: Have you removed the anomalies?

passages.title: Hidey-Hole
passages.text: Excellent work, I'm sure we'll discover more anomalies hiding about, but with your help we've eliminated any immediate threats.

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Southern Kalimdor
passages.text:
Each year, as tribes from southern and central Kalimdor journeyed to Stonetalon to spend the summer season, the rite of the sun blossoms became common practice.

Many saw it as a way to give back to An'she, who worked tirelessly during this long season.

The rite became especially important towards the end of Midsummer, as the southern tribes journeyed back home.

If you're up for another journey, take to the skies once more, my friend, and listen close...

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Southern Kalimdor
passages.text:
As summer came to an end, the final offering of sun blossoms were uplifted to the skies.

Just as the southern tribes returned to their lands, these offerings served as torches to guide An'she home into his season of rest.

Thank you for partaking in these long-forgotten traditions, <name>.

passages.title: Embracing the Infinite Chaos
passages.text: adventurer, make haste to the Infinite Bazaar. I believe you are ready for a new kind of experiment.

passages.title: Embracing the Infinite Chaos
passages.text: Excellent timing, <name>. Now the research can begin.

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Orgrimmar
passages.text:
Midsummer is a time to reflect on the past and future. As old traditions fade, new traditions are born. 

One old tradition, practiced long ago, involved the offering of sun blossoms to An'she. As summer winds took them upwards, the blossoms would burn bright blue and orange.

But faded traditions need not remain lost.

Will you take to the skies to ignite the sun blossoms and help rekindle this old tradition?

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Orgrimmar
passages.text:
You have done our festival a great honor.

It has been many generations since the skies above have been filled with Sun blossoms.

But our celebrations need not be restricted to just the skies of Orgrimmar. All of Kalimdor awaits!

passages.title: Decor Treasure Hunt
passages.text:
Are you ready for today's challenge? I've hidden a piece from my collection here in the neighborhood. To find it, you must merely solve this simple riddle:

Stone laid by lost hands.
Bridging the mountain runoff.
Look where lilies listen.

Good luck!

passages.title: Decor Treasure Hunt
passages.text: Well done!

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Felrunner
passages.text:
In order to better understand the power of both you and your artifact in this timeline we need to undertake some combat studies. It is like social studies, but with blunt force trauma.

This will be a study of fighting the Legion with their own power, so focus on using demonic fel energy to slay your foes.

And remember, this is for the greater good.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Felrunner
passages.text: Remember to pace yourself, the journey is just as important as the destination.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Felrunner
passages.text: Impressive. I can sense your power. This is a most critical addition to our research.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Stormrunner
passages.text:
In order to better understand the power of both you and your artifact in this timeline we need to undertake some combat studies. It is like social studies, but with blunt force trauma.

This will be a study of your attunement to the storm, so focus on fighting opponents by turning the tides quite literally.

And remember, this is for the greater good.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Stormrunner
passages.text: Remember to pace yourself, the journey is just as important as the destination.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Stormrunner
passages.text: Impressive. I can sense your power. This is a most critical addition to our research.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Magerunner
passages.text:
In order to better understand the power of both you and your artifact in this timeline we need to undertake some combat studies. It is like social studies, but with blunt force trauma.

This will be a study of your attunement to the arcane, so focus on fighting opponents with powerful magic.

And remember, this is for the greater good.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Magerunner
passages.text: Impressive. I can sense your power. This is a most critical addition to our research.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Lightrunner
passages.text:
In order to better understand the power of both you and your artifact in this timeline we need to undertake some combat studies. It is like social studies, but with blunt force trauma.

This will be a study of your attunement to the Light, so focus on wielding holy justice to smite your enemies.

And remember, this is for the greater good.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Lightrunner
passages.text: Remember to pace yourself, the journey is just as important as the destination.

passages.title: Infinite Research: Combat Studies, Lightrunner
passages.text: Impressive. I can sense your power. This is a most critical addition to our research.

passages.title: Simply Magical
passages.text:
Who... Who are you? Who sent you? Lilaju?

De cultists massacred our village. I stayed behind to make sure everyone got out.

But de cultists captured me and now dey say dey got somethin' extra special for Idago. I'd rather not find out what.

Dis magic holdin' me here is amateur work. De spells to release de bindings are sure to be in de magical tomes de cultists brought here.

Find de tomes and rip some pages out. Then we can piece together de right words to release me.

passages.title: Simply Magical
passages.text: Appreciate ya, <name>. For freeing me and for keeping an eye on dis one here.

passages.title: Simply Magical
passages.text: De girl's foolishness aside, I owe you my life.

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Northern Eastern Kingdoms
passages.text:
Have you heard the tale of the wildsages and their summer star?

No? Well, you're in for quite the treat!

This story will take you on a journey that follows the path the Wildhammer elders once travelled many moons ago.

Take to the skies and ignite the blossom lights as I tell the tale.

Our journey begins here in the hills of Loch Modan...

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Northern Eastern Kingdoms
passages.text:
"Like a northbound torch across the dark summer sky."

Quite the journey, wasn't it? Now imagine that same path on foot... every summer!

It is quite the popular story for young Wildhammer children.

Some say this tale was what inspired Khardros to settle our people in the Hinterlands after Grim Batol.

Now you too can share this Wildhammer tale by the fireside!

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Southern Eastern Kingdoms
passages.text:
The fire festival is a time for people to come together and share stories around the fire.

One such tale tells of a celebration of Midsummer and the elemental chaos it wrought for the humans of Stormwind.

Our story will take us over the skies of the surrounding regions into lands now scarred by flame and ash.

Take to the skies and ignite the blossom lights as I tell you the story.

It begins in the Burning Steppes...

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Southern Eastern Kingdoms
passages.text: Have you ever wondered why the blossoms of midsummer burn blue and orange? Curious, isn't it?

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Southern Eastern Kingdoms
passages.text:
For many generations, Midsummer bonfires have ignited the summer skies throughout the human lands and beyond.

But even before the kingdom of Stormwind was founded, we dwarves dotted these hills with our festivals of fire.

It is said our first united Midsummer happened by sheer wandering chance during one particularly hot summer long, long ago.

But that, my friend, is another tale. Care for another flight?

passages.title: Wake of the Darkwell
passages.text:
The Sunwell--no... the Darkwell is overrun. 

Void-spawned creatures swarm the regions where our greatest champions of the Light held their ground to the very last.

Champion, can you survey Quel'Danas? Find any survivors? If you tag them with these tokens, our mages here will be able to teleport the individuals back. We must try to save as many as we can.

passages.title: Wake of the Darkwell
passages.text: This is a truly dark day.

passages.title: Wake of the Darkwell
passages.text: So few. But the ones you saved are more than I had hoped for.

passages.title: Addition of Anguish
Honor the Flame
passages.text:
The time of Dawnsummer Festal has long been a cherished season for our people.

Even during the years under the cold grasp of the Ghostlands, the people of Tranquillien strived to maintain this ancient celebration and bring a little light to these once-cold lands.

Now, warmth yourself by the bonfire and honor the flames of summer!

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text: Honor the Tranquillien flame.

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text:
A joyous Midsummer and Dawnsummer Festal upon you, <race>!

While celebrating around the bonfire, it is important to pause for a moment of reflection.

Much has happened here in Silvermoon in recent times and while we cannot dwell upon the darkness of the past, we must look towards the rising Dawn.

Take a moment, while you honor the bonfire, and reflect upon its warmth!

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text: Honor and reflect upon the Silvermoon flame.

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text:
Fetna Alai-nazdo is upon us once again!

Although her trample may be dark, her flame burns brightly in all of us! 

May this turn of the Season burn bright and bring good fortune to you and all who celebrate Fetna Alai-nazdo!

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text: Honor the Zul'Aman flame in honor of Jan'alai!

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text:
I remember the Dawnsummer Festal celebrations back in Eversong and thought 'why not light my own bonfire here in the Howling Ridge?'

Thankfully, the local denizens didn't need much convincing.

I told them the bonfires were sacrificial wells for vessels of esoteric magic and... well, that's one way to describe midsummer blossoms, right?

Will you take a moment and honor the voidflame?

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text: Honor the Voidstorm voidflame.

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text:
The season of Midsummer may be unfamiliar to us, but telling stories by the glow of our root flames is not.

Take a moment to reflect by the bonfire, friend, and listen to those around you.

Ponder that which has come before you and that which has yet to unfurl.

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text: Honor the Harandar flame.

passages.title: Cracked Keystone
passages.text:
Fragmentary images of heroic deeds flash though your mind as you touch the stone, but they fade as fast as they arrive.

Perhaps performing a suitably impressive task will stabilize the stone's magic once more?

passages.title: The Pursuit Continues
passages.text:
I bring word from Magister Umbric!

His apprentice, Leona, has been preoccupied with a desire to learn how the ways of the Illidari.

She apparently found another demon hunter willing to train her, should she prove herself worthy. But after what happened the last time she sought such a mentor, Umbric is concerned for her safety.

Umbric requests you join Leona for this trial. Make sure she is not getting involved in something she is not prepared to handle.

passages.title: The Pursuit Continues
passages.text: Allari seeks to test my resolve. Nothing will deter me from this pursuit.

passages.title: Abhorrent Gauntlet
passages.text:
Leona must demonstrate mastery of her weapons--and of her own enmity--by retrieving undamaged pieces of her kills.

I will observe from here.

You, <name>, will go with her.

passages.title: Abhorrent Gauntlet
passages.text: A demon hunter wields their ire, but is never ruled by it.

passages.title: Abhorrent Gauntlet
passages.text: These parts are pristine. Well done, both of you.

passages.title: Trial of Wrath
passages.text:
Cutting through scores of lesser foes is a simple task for any demon hunter. It's when we face a large, singular threat that our skills are truly tested.

That will be Leona's trial. You will act as her second.

Let us see how she vanquishes a particularly dangerous opponent.

passages.title: Trial of Wrath
passages.text:
The same fire I see in Leona is what brought me where I am today.

She fights well. But more importantly, she has shown me the potential that the void elves possess.

passages.title: Midsummer's Journey to Loch Modan
passages.text:
While Midsummer may be sacred to the tauren, we are not the only people to pay respects to the spirits of fire during the summer months.

The Wildhammer, for example, have shared their own customs with us over the years. It seems this time of year has long been important to the dwarves and denizens of the Eastern Kingdoms.

Journey to their celebration grounds across the sea in Loch Modan and visit with the Wildhammer. 

Perhaps they too will tell you a tale...

passages.title: Midsummer's Journey to Loch Modan
passages.text:
Elder Sunhorn sent you, did he? Well then welcome, <race>, to our Midsummer celebrations!

Care to hear about the origins of the Firefall festival and how the dwarves have celebrated Midsummer?

passages.title: Midsummer's Journey to the Barrens
passages.text:
Although we have our own traditions during this time, we are not the only ones who pay respects to the spirits of fire during the summer months.

If you wish to hear the origins of the tauren traditions, travel to Kalimdor to continue your journey.

passages.title: Midsummer's Journey to the Barrens
passages.text:
Did Aedh Firebeard send you? Well then welcome, <race>, to our Midsummer celebrations!

Care to hear our tale?

passages.title: A Shadowed Journey Through Time
passages.text:
Champion! The curiosities hidden within the Shadowlands are numerous, as are the dangers. I could use some assistance clearing a path, so to speak.

There is much wealth to be gained should you choose to seek it.

passages.title: A Shadowed Journey Through Time
passages.text: Are we in business?

passages.title: A Shadowed Journey Through Time
passages.text: Another prosperous arrangement. You have my thanks.

passages.title: A Shadowed Path Through Time
passages.text:
Old enemies return and battle scars open once more.

Defeat these foes and return with tales of glory.

passages.title: A Shadowed Path Through Time
passages.text: I knew you would return victorious, champion.

passages.title: A Shadowed Path Through Time
passages.text: What news from the war front?

passages.title: The Flickering Anima
passages.text:
The strange anima shimmers with a gentle hum, barely larger than a candle. As your hand draws near it erupts, flooding your mind with a torrent of visions. Triumphs earned through blood, regrets etched in grief, serene stillness all too fleeting, the bitter taste of betrayal. The unbearable cascade threatens to shatter your mind like glass. 

Then, silence. The visions end leaving an image Oribos seared into your mind.

passages.title: The Flickering Anima
passages.text:
<Ta'steld takes the curious anima, studying the wisp as it dances in his hand.>

You were right to bring this to me. As a purveyor of lost curiosities, I know just what to do with this. My thanks, Champion.

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text:
Thrall's parents had lost their life while he was an infant - the start of a rough upbringing. Found by humans, he was raised within the internment camps from the Second War. The one in charge, a man named Blackmoore, was a terribly cruel taskmaster.

A rare friend during that time, Taretha Foxton, promised to help Thrall escape from his shackles.

passages.title: Lorewalking: Rise of the Horde
passages.text:
Let us keep the focus on Thrall, yes?

The Horde's history is expansive - and fascinating. Perhaps we can learn about it another time.

This period denotes the beginning of our hero's restlessness. His time as warchief now over by his own reckoning. Clinging to something he had learned in his journeys, he sought out the Earthen Ring and continued his studies of shamanism. But the life he left behind shadowed him every step of the way...

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text:
The Cataclysm upended both Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. But it is from these wounds where Thrall showed Azeroth what he was truly capable of.

Azeroth needed a Shaman to take care of Deathwing, and they got one.

passages.title: Lorewalking: In Pride's Wake
passages.text:
Thrall left the Horde behind with the hope that the foundation he had laid would lead them towards the future.

Unfortunately turmoil quickly followed - Garrosh, the young orc Thrall had named as warchief, had a very different idea on what the Horde should be. One that left a major scar on Azeroth.

passages.title: Lorewalking: The Weight of Doubt
passages.text:
After Garrosh's death, Thrall found himself doubting his abilities. And so he made a choice - his new path would be his family.

They retreated back into Outland, where his ancestors once lived, and found personal peace. All the while, Azeroth was facing a new war - one that could burn everything he had once fought for to the ground.

passages.title: Lorewalking: In Another's Footsteps
passages.text:
Thrall was at a crossroads, stuck between what he once was and what he should be.

And his hesitation affected more than just his mental state. The elements he once commanded effortlessly barely whispered a response to his call. The hero was held down by his own perception of the past.

But an answer that helped him push forward would come - amusingly, from the same past that haunted him.

passages.title: Lorewalking: Paths Ever Onward
passages.text:
We have just about reached the end of my tale, despite Thrall's story continuing.

It is hard to tell a story that hasn't been finished yet.

But I have no doubt we will continue to see great things from Thrall. Warchief, shaman, hero of Azeroth, Go'el. May he forge forward with all of his names in pride.

passages.title: Bronze Simulacrum
passages.text: <Erus will be delighted to scrap this for you for a heaping sum of bronze.>

passages.title: Bronze Simulacrum
passages.text: You have something for Erus?

passages.title: Bronze Simulacrum
passages.text: YES! Erus will scrap!

passages.title: A Path Forward
passages.text:
<name>, today will be a day of ceremonies and great magic.

Before we begin to cleanse the Darkwell, agreements must be made. 

We have two events that have requested your presence, both as a mediator and as a witness. What we lay down today will have lasting ramifications, and it is important to all of us that we have you at the center of it all. 

Meet with Aethas and Rommath for their respective events. Once you are done, return here and we shall continue to the Darkwell together.

passages.title: A Path Forward
passages.text: You have fought by our side through our darkest hour and during our greatest triumphs. It is only fitting you join us on this day.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Test!
passages.text:
All able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Foreman Eksos in Talador.

The Iron Horde seek to control Talador. The area is perfect to send reinforcements to any other part of Draenor quickly and without resistance.

Foreman Eksos is currently establishing an outpost in Talador. Travel there and stop the Iron Horde.

Glory to the Alliance!

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Stormwind
passages.text:
Welcome to the Midsummer Festival of Fire, friend!

Have you come to toss a few torches? Or maybe dance around the maypole?

Ah, you must be here to ignite the blossom lights over the skies of Stormwind, aren't you? It is an old tradition, long forgotten but newly rekindled!

Well, come on then. Take to the skies and fly!

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Stormwind
passages.text:
It warms me to see the blossoms take to the sky once more.

Stormwind is not the only place you'll see this tradition taking place, of course.

All over the Eastern Kingdoms, blossom lights are floating upwards, waiting to be ignited!

Care for another flight?

passages.title: Echoes Rekindled
passages.text:
The relics you restored still hum with the visions you once walked.

Their stories yearn to be lived again, and each retelling leaves the world just a little richer than before.

Return them to the shrines, let the memories flow, and I shall place in your hands a reward for one who walks the paths of legend.

passages.title: Echoes Rekindled
passages.text:
So be it. 

Once more your path is set, and the relic's truth stands ready to greet you again.

passages.title: By Invitation Only?
passages.text:
Fancy yourself a Brawl'gar contender do you, <class>? They don't let just anyone in there, you know. Certainly not without an invitation.

That said... just between you and me, if you know where to look and you've the means they say anyone can have their moment in the spotlight these days.

passages.title: By Invitation Only?
passages.text:
Looking for a Brawler's Guild invitation are you?

Very hard to come by those, or expensive, or both!

But maybe you and I can work out a deal.

passages.title: The Story of Wey'nan's Ward
passages.text:
You have walked this path before, <name>, yet the Vale of Secrets stirs anew.

The Visionstone awaits, its sacred paintings familiar to your eyes, the handprint at its heart calling for you again.
Press your hand upon it once more and let your spirit be known. The trance will take you as before, carrying your soul through visions whose truths still shift with every telling.

Return to me with what new wisdom the echoes grant you.

passages.title: The Story of Wey'nan's Ward
passages.text: Tell me, <name>,  what new truths did the past reveal this time?

passages.title: The Story of Wey'nan's Ward
passages.text:
Once again you bring me a tale, and even in its retelling I find colors I had not seen before. I will set it into paint beside the first, so that our people may witness every shade of the legend.

Accept this, in gratitude for tending the flame of our history.

I will keep searching the archives, listening for relics whose stories call out to be walked again. Return when the whispers reach you.

passages.title: The Story of the Cauldron of Echoes
passages.text:
Once more, the Cauldron of Echoes stirs.

When I first walked the path of the Zur'Ashar, my master spoke of its place at our beginning. Even they could not grasp its full meaning. Now, it beckons again.

Step into its quiet and draw forth what the ages have hidden. Bring me the truth as it speaks to you this time.

passages.title: The Story of the Cauldron of Echoes
passages.text: So the Cauldron has spoken to you a second time... tell me, what new shapes did the echoes take?

passages.title: The Story of the Cauldron of Echoes
passages.text:
Again, Sai'alyo's shadow takes on new form in your telling, and our history bends toward clarity.

Take this token, as thanks for walking the spiral with me once more.

I will keep listening in the archives for relics whose silence is ready to break. When the world whispers again, find your way back to me.

passages.title: The Story of Aln'hara's Bloom
passages.text:
The bloom still waits, its stillness carrying the same quiet call you once followed.

Yet the bloom's story deepens with each telling. Walk its path again, let the stillness speak anew, and see what more the goddess chooses to share.

passages.title: The Story of Aln'hara's Bloom
passages.text: So, the bloom welcomed you back? Tell me what it spoke this time, and we will guard the memory together.

passages.title: The Story of Aln'hara's Bloom
passages.text:
Again you return with a truth wrapped in gentleness. Aln'hara's voice lingers in the pause between heartbeats, and each time you listen, a new note enters the song.

Accept this, in thanks for tending the quiet places where memory grows.

passages.title: The Story of the Echoless Flame
passages.text:
The Echoless Flame rests as you left it, yet the air around it stirs once more.

You have walked Obayo's path before, felt the echo of that first Shul'ka's purpose. But the past is a shifting thing, and the Flame's silence may yet hide verses you have not heard.
