Return to its vigil. Follow Obayo's steps again, and let the vision show you what remains untold.

passages.title: The Story of the Echoless Flame
passages.text: Tell me, <name>, what new light did the flame cast for you this time?

passages.title: The Story of the Echoless Flame
passages.text:
Again the Flame yields its truth to you, and again the tale twists in the telling. Morta'ka the Sundered Echo looms no less large, yet fresh details sharpen the memory and deepen the weight of what was lost.

Take this with my thanks for stoking the embers of a story long gone cold. When next the silence breaks, we will be ready to listen together.

passages.title: The Story of Russula's Outreach
passages.text:
The spear still waits where you last left it, pale threads of mushroom slowly weaving new patterns into its grain.

The culling grounds draw you again. Walk their softened paths, follow what spores still rise, and let the visions show what time has chosen to reveal this season.

passages.title: The Story of Russula's Outreach
passages.text: What shape did the tale take this time? Tell me, and we will fold this telling into the many before it.

passages.title: The Story of Russula's Outreach
passages.text:
You have tended the memory well, <name>.

Take this token of thanks. When the land calls -- as it always does -- return. Even mercy has layers yet to be uncovered.

passages.title: The Story of the Root of the World
passages.text:
The Root of the World stands as it did before--ancient, unbowed--yet the soil breathes differently today. Beneath your feet, the pulse of Harandar quickens, as though eager to share another verse of its oldest story.

You have seen through Ruilla the Huntress's eyes once before. But the Rootways are never walked the same way twice. Go again, and let the land decide which truths it will show you now.

passages.title: The Story of the Root of the World
passages.text: And so the Root yielded another fragment? Tell me, what shade of truth did it whisper this time?

passages.title: The Story of the Root of the World
passages.text:
Once more the Root speaks through Ruilla's memory, and once more the lesson comes wrapped in both pride and sorrow. She remains the first Rootwarden, the first to walk those hidden ways, but fresh details now cling to her legend like moss to stone.

Your return is a gift to the land as much as to me, <name>. When the soil shifts again beneath your steps, we will listen together.

passages.title: The Story of Sky's Hope
passages.text:
Sky's Hope rests in its cradle as before, yet the heavens above seem sharper tonight.

You have traced Awe'ohna's path once, but the tale shifts with every telling. Walk the path again, and perhaps the sky will tilt just so, revealing a truth you missed before.

passages.title: The Story of Sky's Hope
passages.text:
Again the sky has turned in your favor, <name>, and again Awe'ohna's story greets you with both clarity and mystery.

When the firmament stirs once more, I trust you'll be ready to walk under it with me again.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text:
Well <class>, it's your lucky day. I just happen to have an extremely genuine Brawler's Guild Invitation right here in my stockpile.

That said I'll need a moment to process the paperwork. That requires my complete concentration without your prying eyes on me. So do please give me a moment.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text:
Here's your extremely genuine Brawler's Guild Invitation.

Please note all sales are final.

There will be no refunds, or receipts.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text: Some of the lines look a little crooked.

passages.title: A Letter for Adventure
passages.text:
<You look down to see a rough looking letter with your name on it.

Why not open it up to see what's inside?>

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Silvermoon
passages.text:
The season of Midsummer is celebrated by many cultures across Azeroth.

Even now, bonfires across the land are ignited in honor of the spirits of fire.

To share our customs with all who dwell under the sun's warmth, I've had crates of sun blossoms brought to Silvermoon.

Take to the skies and ignite the blossoms above, <name>!

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Silvermoon
passages.text:
The citizens of Silvermoon were quite enthused by your aerial display over the city.

Even the dragonhawks seemed to enjoy the glow of the blossoms overhead.

Thank you for bringing joy to so many during this summer festival.

The spirits of fire and An'she himself will be pleased.

passages.title: Lorewalking: The Loa of Kings
passages.text:
Where to begin? There's so much to say!

There's a great story from the Zandalari about the connection between troll and loa. Let's start there!

passages.title: Lorewalking: The Loa of Kings
passages.text: With Rezan defeated, King Rastakhan was in big trouble. He was wounded far deeper than any physical strike, as his connection to health and longevity were both ripped away.

passages.title: Lorewalking: Death of the Drakkari Loa
passages.text:
The Drakkari of Zul'Drak are well known for massacring their loa. The prophets of the Drakkari loa decided to take the full power of the loa by force.

The loa were blind-sided by this betrayal. They never dreamed rituals existed that could permanently kill them and steal their essence.

passages.title: Lorewalking: Death of the Drakkari Loa
passages.text: The Drakkari empire crumbled after Gundrak fell. It couldn't recover from the turn into darkness and the aftermath that followed.

passages.title: Lorewalking: The Blood Loa
passages.text:
Not every loa is a protector and companion to trolls. There are loa that eat their followers, like the blood loa, Hakkar. In trade for sacrifices, Hakkar grants dark blood powers to his followers. But he always takes more than he gives.

Hakkar the Soulflayer has absorbed so much blood from his cultists that he's become almost a perpetual threat to the world.

passages.title: Lorewalking: The Hash'ey
passages.text:
The last story I want to share is about the Darkspear trolls... and Mueh'zala.

Mueh'zala is a mighty Loa of Death. Highly manipulative, he puts his plans into motion by using others as his pawns.

He's used a hash'ey in the past. A hash'ey is a troll imbued with the full power of the loa.

passages.title: Lorewalking: The Hash'ey
passages.text:
Both loa and troll have tried to force the bond of the hash'ey, but the strongest bonds are when they work together.

There's so much to learn about the loa. I'm still collecting their stories, but this was a good start!

passages.title: Reignite the Skies: Stormwind
passages.text:
Welcome to the Midsummer Festival of Fire, friend! 

Have you come to toss a few torches? Or maybe dance around the maypole?

Ah, you must be here to ignite the blossom lights over the skies of Stormwind, aren't you? It is an old tradition, long forgotten but newly rekindled!

Well, come on then, take to the skies and fly!

passages.title: Reignite the Skies: Stormwind
passages.text:
It warms me to see the blossoms take to the sky once more.

Stormwind is not the only place you'll see this tradition taking place, of course.

All over the Eastern Kingdoms, blossom lights are floating upwards, waiting to be ignited!

passages.title: Reignite the Skies: Orgrimmar
passages.text:
Midsummer is a time to reflect on the past and future. As old traditions fade, new traditions are born. 

One old tradition, practiced long ago, involved the offering of sun blossoms to An'she. As summer winds took them upwards, the blossoms would burn bright blue and orange.

But faded traditions need not remain lost.

Will you take to the skies to ignite the sun blossoms and help rekindle this old tradition?

passages.title: Reignite the Skies: Orgrimmar
passages.text:
You have done our festival a great honor.

It has been many generations since the skies above have been filled with Sun blossoms.

But our celebrations need not be restricted to just the skies of Orgrimmar. All of Kalimdor awaits!

passages.title: By Invitation Only?
passages.text:
Fancy yourself a Brawlpub contender do you, <class>? They don't let just anyone in there, you know. Certainly not without an invitation.

That said... just between you and me, if you know where to look and you've the means they say anyone can have their moment in the spotlight these days.

passages.title: By Invitation Only?
passages.text:
Looking for a Brawler's Guild invitation are you?

Very hard to come by those, or expensive, or both!

But maybe you and I can work out a deal.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text:
Well <class>, it's your lucky day. I just happen to have an extremely genuine Brawler's Guild Invitation right here in my stockpile.

That said I'll need a moment to process the paperwork. That requires my complete concentration without your prying eyes on me. So do please give me a moment.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text:
Here's your extremely genuine Brawler's Guild Invitation.

Please note all sales are final.

There will be no refunds, or receipts.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text: Some of the lines look a little crooked.

passages.title: Ta'readon's Mount Voucher
passages.text: This token bears the seal of Overseer Ta'readon in Oribos. They would be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Ta'readon's Mount Voucher
passages.text: I see you have served our merchants admirably. Accept one of our finest steeds as a reward.

passages.title: Understanding the War Within
passages.text:
I fear your time in Valdrakken must come to an end.

Dark forces gather to threaten other parts of Azeroth. We will do what we can to uncover Iridikron's schemes.

You must learn more of what has unfolded.

passages.title: Understanding the War Within
passages.text: <The tome floats in front of you. Its pages are filled with knowledge of all that has happened.>

passages.title: Amani Answers
passages.text:
My uncle has already started communin' with de loa to find information on dis Ula'tek. Meanwhile, we gonna dig through his boxes to see what we can find.

<Zul'jan points to all the boxes scattered around the terrace.>

My uncle has de biggest collection of histories among de Amani. I used to read through dem when I was a boy.

Look for anything about Ula'tek, snakes, or early Amani history. I'll take these, you search de others.

passages.title: Amani Answers
passages.text: What does dis mask know?

passages.title: Amani Answers
passages.text: Did you hear what it said? A weapon!

passages.title: A Call for Aid
passages.text:
<name>, I call upon you to aid the Amani again as a fellow hash'ura. Another dire threat is upon them.

Malacrass has returned.

Witherbark Bluffs is under attack by a monstrous enemy the likes of which I have never seen. And with our brush against the Twilight's Blade, the timing could not be worse.

Zul'jan deserted us and... we believe he may be at least partially at fault.

We will deal with both of them in time. For now, help us before we are overrun.

passages.title: A Call for Aid
passages.text:
Thank the Light you are here.

We have work to do.

passages.title: Saving Those Bound
passages.text:
<Liadrin wipes sweat from her brow and addresses you without turning. You see minor cuts and scrapes she has neglected to heal.>

We fell back from the town gates. There were so many wounded and poisoned. Orweyna, Tak'lejo, and I best serve the Amani here.

But you should be out there helping Zul'jarra.

Malacrass's serpents are capturing Witherbark, coiling around them, and filling them with poison.

Free them--and make sure to find Dak'zor. He was on the front line and first to fall.

passages.title: Saving Those Bound
passages.text: Move, <name>! Before we lose more Amani!

passages.title: Saving Those Bound
passages.text:
Dey took Dak'zor away to de east?

<Zul'jarra growls.>

Toward de strait. Toward de isle. What do dey want with him there?

Spirit or no, I'll find a way to get my hands 'round dat Hex Lord's throat...

passages.title: All Bark, All Bite
passages.text:
The wounds I have seen... the ferocity.

Not only do these serpents slither on the ground and coil around our warriors' bodies, but they cut deep with their poisoned blades and target them with their talons as they dive from the skies.

Zul'jarra and her forces cannot win this on their own, but my hands are needed here. 

Help Zul'jarra by taking them down.

passages.title: All Bark, All Bite
passages.text: Never liked snakes... and dis mess is not helpin'.

passages.title: All Bark, All Bite
passages.text:
De battle is turnin' in our favor thanks to you, but de fight is not done.

We got some breathin' room now, but we got to strike at de source--Malacrass--before more snakes start crawlin' all over us.

passages.title: Down With the Skies
passages.text:
I will need some time to call upon Akil'zon and open de way. Dat's where you come in.

Protect me, my hash'ura.

I entrust you with my life. We've taken great leaps before, eh?

passages.title: Down With the Skies
passages.text: De loa can't come with us? Then we will have to rely on our own strength.

passages.title: To the Skybridge
passages.text:
<Zul'jarra's face is dark with rage as she looks off toward the Skybridge.>

Zul'jan... you let dat snake Malacrass taint your mind and heart. For what? Power?

De lightwood was one thing. But dis?

I don't know what Malacrass has planned for de captives, but we have to take de fight to him and away from our people.

Follow de monsters' path back to de Skybridge. I will consult de loa and meet you there.

With their help, we will stop this.

passages.title: To the Skybridge
passages.text: I will make my way to Malacrass, even if I have to rip de scales off a thousand of these monsters.

passages.title: Those Who Can't Fight
passages.text: Zal'jarra also asks us to rescue a few people!
